xml-to-json.quickAnswer: Paste XML and this tool converts it to JSON on the spot: attributes become @-prefixed keys, nested elements become nested objects, repeated sibling tags become arrays, and mixed text lands in a #text key. The result is valid, pretty-printed JSON you can copy or download.
keyFacts: XML and JSON both describe structured data but with different syntax rules.
XML attributes have no direct JSON equivalent, so this tool prefixes them with @.
Repeated sibling elements (like multiple <book> tags) naturally become JSON arrays.
Text mixed with child elements is kept under the #text key so nothing is lost.
Conversion is structural only; it does not change the meaning of your data.
howTo: Paste your XML document into the editor.
Watch the JSON output update instantly.
Check that repeated elements became arrays as expected.
Copy the JSON or download it as converted.json.
Use the sample button to see the mapping rules in action.
benefits: Instant conversion with no uploads or waiting.
Attributes, arrays, and mixed content handled sensibly.
Output is valid JSON with clean 2-space indentation.
Runs fully offline in your browser.
limitations: Values stay strings: "29.99" is not auto-converted to a number.
Namespaces are kept as literal prefixes, not resolved.
Comments and processing instructions are dropped.
CDATA is treated as plain text.

faqs.a: With an @ prefix: id="bk101" becomes "@id": "bk101". This is a common convention that keeps attributes distinct from child elements.
Two or more siblings with the same tag name become a JSON array. A single child stays a plain object.
Yes. The output is built with JSON.stringify, so it always parses with JSON.parse in any language.

faqs.q: Why are numbers quoted as strings?
faqs.a: XML has no type information, so the converter keeps everything as strings. Convert types in your own code after parsing.

faqs.q: Can I convert JSON back to XML?
faqs.a: This tool is one-way. For the reverse direction, build XML from your JSON with a small script or a dedicated converter.

xml-to-json.assumptionNote: Mapping: attributes use the @ prefix, mixed text uses #text, repeated siblings become arrays. Values stay strings.
